title: observability: automate Prometheus/Grafana + log shipping for Private installs (helm + terraform + upgrade hooks)
author: Aisha Raman
description: Automate provisioning and upgrade/rollback for the observability stack in Private installs. This PR adds a Terraform module and Helm chart integration to deploy Prometheus, Alertmanager, Grafana (provisioned dashboards and datasources), and a lightweight log-shipping pipeline (Fluent Bit) as an optional component in the private-installer. Motivation: customers deploying Redwood Private were repeatedly performing manual wiring of monitoring and dashboards during installs and upgrades; this PR codifies a repeatable, idempotent flow with clear upgrade hooks and rollback behavior. Changes include: reusable terraform module (outputs: prometheus_endpoint, grafana_url, tls certs), opinionated Helm values and templates for the redwood-observability umbrella chart, Grafana provisioning for key dashboards (ingesters, request-latency, token-cost), Prometheus alerting rules for node/memory/cpu and redwood-specific SLO regressions, Fluent Bit DaemonSet and CRD mappings for log forwarding to user-configured sinks, and installer lifecycle hooks (pre-upgrade validation, post-upgrade smoke checks, and rollback cleanup). The description below lists the checkboxes that were validated during testing. CHECKLIST: [x] Terraform module with examples (GCP/AWS/VPC) [x] Helm umbrella chart and values schema [x] Grafana dashboards packaged and provisioned via configmaps [x] Prometheus rules and recording rules [x] Fluent Bit config and optional parsing rules [x] Installer hooks for apply/rollback + idempotency tests [x] Upgrade e2e smoke in CI [x] Documentation updates and example Linear tickets referenced. Risk and compatibility notes: feature is gated behind a boolean in the installer config (enable_observability: true) and has sensible defaults so it is opt-in for existing customers. No breaking API changes to installer control plane. Follow-up work: add RBAC policy bundle to restrict Grafana admin, add OIDC integration to Grafana, and expand alert runbooks in SLO playbooks.
commits: add(terraform): observability module + examples; add(helm): redwood-observability umbrella chart + grafana provisioning; add(logging): fluent-bit DaemonSet and parsers; add(prometheus): alerting & recording rules; feat(installer): pre/post upgrade hooks and idempotency checks; fix(values): default tls/ingress values; docs: add observability guide and upgrade notes; ci: e2e smoke for private-installer observability
review_comments: Miguel Torres: Overall looks great. A few nits: can we tighten the default retention on Prometheus metrics to 15d instead of 30d and make it configurable? Also ensure the grafana provisioning configmaps are not mounted with cluster-admin secrets.

Aisha Raman: + Updated default retention to 15d and exposed prometheus.retentionDays in values.schema.json. Grafana provisioning was changed to use a read-only service account and we added notes in docs about minimum RBAC necessary.
Samir Patel: Please add an explicit smoke check for alertmanager routing in the post-upgrade hook and fail fast if silences are blocking critical alerts.

Aisha Raman: Added alertmanager-route check in observability-post-upgrade-smoke.sh; the script will now exit non-zero on critical alert blocking and the installer will trigger a rollback path as documented.
Jillian Wong: CI flakes on the helm provisioning test — looks like a race when provisioning dashboards. Can we add retry logic in the test and a short backoff?
Aisha Raman: Added retry/backoff to provisioning_test.go and increased the provisioning timeout in CI for this job. Re-ran CI and the job passed.
release_notes: Added optional observability automation for Private installs: Terraform module and Helm umbrella chart to deploy Prometheus, Alertmanager, Grafana (with provisioned dashboards), and Fluent Bit log shipping. Installer hooks added for safe upgrades and rollbacks. Opt-in via enable_observability flag. See docs/private-installer/observability.md for configuration and examples.
upgrade_instructions: To enable on an existing Private install: 1) set enable_observability: true in your installer config and provide required tfvars (s3/gcs bucket or cloud storage for prometheus remote write if used), 2) run terraform apply in terraform/modules/observability with the same state backend as your installer, 3) run installer apply which will deploy Helm chart and run post-upgrade smoke checks. Rollback: installer will run observability-post-upgrade-smoke.sh; if smoke fails the installer will automatically trigger the observability-pre-upgrade rollback steps which remove new resources created by the Helm release. For manual rollback: helm rollback <release> and terraform destroy -target=module.observability. Detailed steps in docs/private-installer/upgrade-observability.md.
